title: Log smoothness with invertible chart torsion preserves log regularity
statement: Let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fine saturated log schemes in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Suppose $(Y,M_Y)$ is log regular in the stratum and dimension sense of that definition. Assume that etale locally on source and target there are compatible fs charts $A\to M_Y$, $B\to M_X$ and a homomorphism $h:A\to B$ for which $h^{\rm gp}$ is injective, the torsion subgroup of its cokernel is finite of order invertible on the source, and the induced scheme morphism $X\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[A]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[B]$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Here $\mathbf Z[C]$ denotes the monoid ring, free as an abelian group on symbols $z^c$ with $z^cz^{c\prime}=z^{c+c\prime}$. This is the chart meaning of log smooth in this statement. Then $(X,M_X)$ is log regular in the same sense. In particular the cokernel in the chart condition is allowed to have nonzero torsion of invertible order; it need not be torsion-free.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.8, printed p.70 (log smooth over log regular implies log regular); chart interpretation as in Expose XVI, Proposition 3.6.3, printed p.252.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point of $X$ and choose the compatible chart neighbourhoods in the hypothesis; write them again as $X,Y$. Put $P=A$, $Q=B$, $h:P\to Q$, and let $n$ be the positive order of the torsion subgroup of $Q^{\rm gp}/h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})$. Although $n$ is only assumed invertible on the source, its image is nonzero in the residue field of our source point, hence also in the residue field of its image in $Y$. Restrict $Y$ to its open locus where $n$ is invertible and restrict $X$ to its inverse image. This retains the point and the charts and smooth comparison. The geometric-stalk definition [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] shows directly that restricting a log regular scheme to these neighbourhoods retains log regularity. It suffices to prove the result on such neighbourhoods: an etale neighbourhood of a geometric point has the same strict local ring and log stalk at that point, since the pointed etale neighbourhoods defining that stalk refine each other.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.2, p.69; pointwise reduction for VI 1.8, p.70.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-fs-chart-torsion-factorization] to $h:P\to Q$. It gives the explicit fs monoid $R=\{q\in Q:\exists m>0,\ mq\in h(P)\}$ and a factorization $P\xrightarrow{a}R\xrightarrow{b}Q$. The first map is Kummer and has injective group map with finite cokernel of order $n$, annihilated by $n$; the second has injective group map with torsion-free cokernel. These conclusions include group-completion torsion and do not require sharp charts.

source.place: VI 1.8 and 2.1, pp.70--71; agent-supplied saturation factorization using VIII 3.1.17, p.101.

proof.text: Form $Y_R=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]$. First, local Noetherianity: on an affine chart $Y=\operatorname{Spec}D$ the affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives the ring $D\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[R]$. If $r_1,\ldots,r_s$ generate $R$, this is a quotient of $D[T_1,\ldots,T_s]$ by the surjective map $T_i\mapsto1\otimes z^{r_i}$: each tensor is a sum of $d\otimes z^{\sum e_i r_i}=d\prod_i(1\otimes z^{r_i})^{e_i}$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Now give $Y_R$ the log structure $L_{Y_R}(R,\beta)$ associated to $\beta:R\to\Gamma(Y_R,\mathcal O)$, $r\mapsto 1\otimes z^r$ [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]; its stalk formula says exactly that $R$ is a chart in the sense of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], so $Y_R$ is fs because $R$ is fs. On $Y$ the chart identifies $M_Y$ with $L_Y(P)$, and the universal property of [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] (applied on $Y_R$ to the inverse image, $[p,u]\mapsto[a(p),u]$) gives the map of log structures of $Y_R\to Y$ with chart $a:P\to R$. Its comparison with this very same fibre product is the identity, hence etale. Its finite group cokernel is annihilated by $n$, which is invertible on $Y$ by step 1. Thus every hypothesis of [lem-per-invertible-kummer-chart-log-regular] holds, and $Y_R$ is log regular.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; VI 1.8, p.70. Noetherianity: Stacks Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text:
The original $Q$-chart on $X$ and $b:R\to Q$ induce a log morphism $X\to Y_R$: on functions the new $R$-monomials are sent to their $Q$-monomials. Its compatible map of log structures comes from [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]: the inverse image of $L_{Y_R}(R)$ maps to $L_X(R)$ by $[r,u]\mapsto[r,u]$, and the universal property of $L_X(R)$ turns the monoid map $R\xrightarrow{b}Q\to M_X(X)$, compatible with the structure maps to $\mathcal O_X$, into a map $L_X(R)\to M_X$; by construction $R\to Q$ is a compatible chart map for $X\to Y_R$. Its comparison target is canonically the original target, since
$$\left(Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]\right)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]\cong Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q].$$
Indeed both fibre-product universal properties specify precisely a map to $Y$ and a compatible map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$; the map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[R]$ is forced by $b$. This identification sends the comparison of $X\to Y_R$ to the given smooth comparison of $f$. Now apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] to $X\to Y_R$, with its fs charts $R,Q$: both schemes are locally Noetherian, $Y_R$ is log regular by step 3, $b^{\rm gp}$ is injective with torsion-free cokernel by step 2, and the comparison is smooth as just checked. Its log-regularity conclusion gives log regularity at our chosen point of $X$. Repeating step 1 at every geometric point proves the assertion, including the vacuous empty-source case. No torsion-freeness of the original cokernel has been imposed.

source.place: VI 1.8, p.70, reduced to the Kummer case VI 2.2 and the existing torsion-free chart theorem by an explicit fibre-product identification.

proof_origin.place: VI 1.8, p.70, and VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72; factorization through the root saturation of the chart image. ILO only cites Kato 1994, 8.2 for the general preservation theorem; this split supplies a different algebraic reduction using existing DAG tools.

Step 1: n invertible at x implies invertible at f(x), since kappa(f(x)) embeds in kappa(x); restricting to D(n) keeps the charts, the comparison and log regularity, which is checked pointwise at geometric points. Step 2: uses only what the new node states. Step 3: checked each hypothesis of lem-per-invertible-kummer-chart-log-regular (fs and locally Noetherian, where finite type comes from the monomial generators via the 01I4 node and 00FN; a injective; Kummer; finite cokernel annihilated by n, invertible on Y; identity comparison is etale). Step 4: checked each hypothesis of lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular (b^gp injective with torsion-free cokernel Q^gp/H; smooth comparison through the pasted fibre products). New node lem-per-fs-chart-torsion-factorization: proved it myself. R^gp=H by the trick n(g+p2)=p1+(n-1)p2; R is saturated in H; R is finitely generated as the saturation of h(P) plus coset representatives, via lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation. Tested on N->N with 1->n, N->Z, N->N^2, 0->finite group and the identity: true. Not a duplicate of trf fs-chart-free-factorization (torsion-free cokernel), fine-monoid-finite-saturation (saturates in the monoid's own group) or log-regular-toric-refinement (P^gp=Q^gp), and not a restatement of the item. Both accepted, and the added node is generic and already in that closure. lean.statement: theorem logSmooth_invertibleTorsion_logRegular (X Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (f : EtaleLogHom X Y) (hY : Y.IsLogRegular) (hcharts : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme), ∃ c : InvertibleTorsionFSLogChart X Y f, Nonempty ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale t).fiber.obj c.V) ∧ Smooth c.comparison) : X.IsLogRegular
